chapter: Faith, study and the Chicago scene
title: Daddy O' Daylie, Sid McCoy and the failed record-deal attempt
summary: Chicago DJs hear his trio but nothing comes of a record deal, so he heads for New York.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Sid McCoy. He had a show called… …he was one of the great jazz DJs in Chicago, called, "The Real McCoy" and he had his theme song was, "The Real McCoy" by Frank Sinatra and then he'd come on. He had this smooth voice and he'd say, "Hey, hey, Old Bean, and you too baby! It's the Real McCoy!" He used to come and hear me and Daddy O' used to come and hear me, because I think Daddy O’ discovered Ramsey...

So I had this trio with Ernest McCarty and a drummer name Butch McCass and we played at this supper club out on 75th and I was trying to see… Sid and Daddy O’ came around to hear me play, and I was trying to see if I could get a record deal out of them, and nothing came of it so I eventually left and came to New York. I had exhausted everything in Chicago that I had, but let us go back.
